title: Embrace Difficulties
heading: Embrace Difficulties
coreClaim: The chapter argues that some hard-feeling learning methods work better because they force retrieval, generation, recovery, or repair, but difficulty only helps when it preserves a real learning mechanism and enough support.
distinctMechanism: The mechanism is desirable difficulty: challenge that strengthens memory or transfer through reconstruction and correction rather than through pain alone.
requiredAnchors: Hard-feeling practice can help when it pressures retrieval or generation.
Errorless ease is not always best for durable learning.
Useful errors need correction and support.
commonMisreadings: Errors are useful even without repair.
specificApplications: Use low-stakes generation and retrieval during review.
Treat mistakes as repair opportunities when feedback follows.
Design challenge with enough support that the learner can still recover.
hardEdgeRequirement: Keep the line between productive challenge and overload visible.
thresholdQuestion: When does difficulty still teach, and when does it strip away too much support to help?
